newsitem.title: UK: Alliance & Leicester leads bank sector higher.
newsitem.headline: Alliance & Leicester leads bank sector higher.

text.p: Shares in newly floated Alliance & Leicester Plc advanced to a record on Friday, leading UK bank shares higher, amid a general shortage of stock in the market and bid speculation, dealers said.
A report in the Financial Times said Royal Bank of Scotland would be an "obvious takeover target" for HSBC Holdings, bolstering the group, they said.
There also was talk that Barclays Plc or National Westminster Bank Plc might bid for A&L, they said.
At 0746 GMT, A&L shares were up 22-1/2p, or 3.6 percent, to 649, having climbed as high as 657.
HSBC shares were up 4p to 1799, just 2p off the record set initially. The shares surged by more than five percent on Thursday.
Shares in Standard Chartered Plc, Abbey National Plc, Bank of Scotland and Lloyds TSB Group Plc also scored new record highs.
Standard shares were up 3p to 983-1/2p; Abbey National shares advanced 7p to 891-1/2; shares in Bank of Scotland climbed 3-1/2p to 413-1/2p and Lloyds shares added 3p to 605-1/2.
NatWest shares surged 11-1/2p to 796-1/2, while shares in Royal Bank of Scotland leapt 21p to 623-1/2. Shares in and Lloyds firmed 3p to 605-1/2.
"This market is getting very frothy," one dealer said.

Another dealer, who wasn't forecasting a significant correction in the sector until this summer's building societies flotations, said the shares have almost become too expensive to attract takeover bids.

"But the speculation will continue," the dealer said. "The bank sector has really overheated, but with Halifax (flotation) coming up, I think there are still more (gains) to come." --London Newsroom +44 171 542 5106
